title: [C++][CI] Have a job with ARROW_LARGE_MEMORY_TESTS enabled
body:
### Describe the enhancement requested

Currently, the C++ large memory tests do not seem exercised on any CI platform (except perhaps some R build? it's not really clear).

We should make sure those are exercised on at least one CI configuration, probably Crossbow-driven. We will certainly need a specific runner for that.

We might even discover that some of those tests are currently broken...

### Component(s)

C++, Continuous Integration

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Some observations:
* the "large memory" test in `arrow-array-test` (actually `array_list_test.cc`) perhaps doesn't deserve to be marked as such
* `parquet-arrow-test` is extremely slow in debug mode without optimizations; because of this, we need to enable either `-Og` (faster) or `-O1` (even faster)
* the tests all fit in less than 32 GB, though 64 GB would be more comfortable IMHO

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Frequent disruptions would mean we would have trouble starting or finishing test jobs, which would make for noisy or expensive on-demand CI.
For instance m5-4xlarge have frequent disruptions, but we use them for benchmarks. Because they often get interrupted we [set them 80% on-demand](https://github.com/arctosalliance/arrow-benchmarks-ci/blob/bc8c3caa51f3d4fe7777b24f07f4a7fca9476123/terraform/buildkite_agents.tf#L356) just to have regular completiions. That's why I would pick a machine with rare interruptions.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Disruption is only for spot instances?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: Yes, spot instances are spare unused computing capacity available at discount to on-demand. Providers can reclaim them with e.g. a two-minute warning.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Ok, so why is it a problem if we use on-demand?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: On demand is 3x the price.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: So can you read https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/46600#issuecomment-4031683495?
